::api-operation{method="POST" path="/v1/businesses/{biz}/payment_intents/{pi}/authorize"}
#docs
⚠️ **Test mode only.** This route DECIDES that the buyer passed the challenge, by force-resolving it at the simulated gateway. A real gateway makes that decision itself and reports it over its webhook, so a live business gets a 400 here: an intent marked `authorized` locally while the gateway still considers the buyer unauthenticated would let the next capture take money the issuer never approved.

## Path parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `biz` | `string` | **yes** | Business id (biz_…) |
| `pi` | `string` | **yes** | Payment intent id (pi_…) |

## Headers

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Idempotency-Key` | `string` | no | Safely retry writes — repeats return the original response. If a write FAILED after it had already taken effect, that failure is what repeats: the key is spent, and a new attempt needs a new key. |

## Response

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `object` | `string` | The object type; always `payment_intent`. One of `payment_intent`. |
| `id` | `string` | The payment intent's id (pi_…). |
| `status` | `string` | `voided` is set by the void route alongside `voided_at`. One of `inited`, `in_progress`, `authorized`, `consumed`, `expired`, `voided`. |
| `purpose` | `string` | Whether the intent takes a payment or saves a payment method. One of `payment`, `setup`. |
| `amount_minor` | `integer` | Always 0 for a `setup` intent. |
| `max_amount_minor` | `integer` | The mandate ceiling this `setup` intent registered with, and what a retry re-registers with. Null for `payment` intents. |
| `currency` | `string` | The payment intent's currency (ISO-4217 code). |
| `attempt_count` | `integer` | Payment attempts — how many times this intent has been tried at the gateway. |
| `last_attempt_status` | `string` | Status of the NEWEST attempt. `status` above cannot express a refusal — there is no `failed` intent status, because a declined authorization leaves the intent OPEN so it can be retried — so this is what distinguishes a declined intent from one the buyer is still working through. `null` means no attempt has been made yet. One of `inited`, `requires_action`, `authorized`, `consumed`, `failed`, `voided`. |
| `next_action` | `object` | How the buyer completes the challenge, when one is outstanding. |
| `expires_at` | `string · ISO-8601` | When the intent expires (ISO-8601 UTC). |
| `voided_at` | `string · ISO-8601` | When the intent was voided (ISO-8601 UTC), or null. |
| `created_at` | `string · ISO-8601` | When the payment intent was created (ISO-8601 UTC). |
| `resource_version` | `integer` | A number that goes up on every change. |

## Status codes

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | Success |
| `400` | Live business (use the gateway webhook), or intent not authorizable |
| `404` | No such payment intent |
| `409` | Idempotency-Key conflict — the key is already in flight, or was reused with a different request payload. |

#request
```bash [Request]
curl -X POST "$TMBILLING_URL/v1/businesses/biz_XXXXXXXXXXXX01/payment_intents/pi_XXXXXXXXXXXX01/authorize" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TMBILLING_API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)"
```
